svg.title: Firewall rule example, the order rules are checked, and how VMs reach the internet and Google services
svg.desc: Left: an example from the enterprise foundations blueprint of two rules in a network firewall policy. Rule 2 is an ingress rule that allows traffic from instances tagged service=frontend to instances tagged service=backend at priority 999. Rule 1 is an egress rule that denies outbound traffic from all sources at priority 65530. Traffic from instance-1 to instance-2 matches Rule 2; only Rule 1 matches traffic to instance-3, so it is denied. Below that, the default order in which Google Cloud checks rules, from hierarchical firewall policies down to the implied action, and a network setting that can move the network firewall policies before the VPC firewall rules. Right: outbound internet access through Cloud NAT, inbound internet access through Cloud Load Balancing with Google Cloud Armor, direct internet access to a VM marked not recommended, Google services reached through a Private Service Connect endpoint on TCP port 443 with Private Google Access on every subnet, and the rules of the hierarchical firewall policy.
svg.text: Example: two rules in a network firewall policy
From tag service=frontend to tag service=backend
Only Rule 1 matches traffic to instance-3.
Default order for each VPC network
A network setting can move steps 4 and 5 before step 3.
The blueprint does not use these
Ingress to a VM: deny. Egress: allow.
Internet access and Google services in the blueprint
The blueprint allows no inbound or outbound traffic between its VPC networks
and the internet. For workloads that need it, the blueprint recommends the options below.
For finer control, Secure Web Proxy allows only trusted web services.
Direct connectivity between the internet and a VM through an external IP
Private Google Access is on for every subnet.
Firewall policies and DNS records allow traffic to the endpoint.
Used together, these controls allow a private path to Google Cloud services,
without relying on internet outbound traffic.
Hierarchical firewall policy rules in the blueprint
Ingress allow TCP ports 22, 3389 from 35.235.240.0/20: IAP for TCP forwarding
Ingress allow TCP ports 80, 443 from four Google ranges: health checks
Egress allow TCP port 1688 to 35.190.247.13/32: Windows server activation
Private address ranges (RFC 1918), in and out: go to next
Go to next: continues with the next folder policy, or the next step
